questions.question: Which fungal pathogen has been found to use chromosome alterations to resist common antifungal drugs like fluconazole and voriconazole?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Candida tropicalis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Candida tropicalis** is a significant fungal pathogen that has been found to utilize **chromosome alterations**, specifically **aneuploidy** and **segmental duplications**, to develop resistance against common antifungal medications.
 
• This pathogen is particularly known for resisting **fluconazole** and **voriconazole**, which are the primary **azole** drugs used in clinical settings to treat yeast infections.
 
• Research indicates that by altering the number of **chromosomes** or duplicating specific regions of the **genome**, the fungus can increase the expression of genes like **ERG11** and **efflux pumps**, which help the cell survive in the presence of toxic drug concentrations.
 
• Unlike **Candida albicans**, which is the most common species, **Candida tropicalis** is frequently associated with higher **virulence** and **mortality rates** in certain geographical regions.
 
• The ability to undergo rapid **genomic rearrangements** allows this fungus to adapt to the **host environment** and medical interventions much faster than through simple point mutations alone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Prevalence:** **Candida tropicalis** is highly prevalent in **tropical** and **subtropical countries**, including **India**, **Brazil**, and parts of **Southeast Asia**, where it is often the second or third most common cause of **invasive candidiasis**.
 
• **Mechanism of Azoles:** Drugs like **Fluconazole** and **Voriconazole** work by inhibiting the **CYP51** (or **ERG11**) enzyme, which is essential for the synthesis of **ergosterol**, a vital component of the fungal **cell membrane**.
 
• **Comparison with other Pathogens:**
 
 
• **Candida albicans:** While it also uses **aneuploidy** (specifically **Isochromosome 5L**), the question highlights **Candida tropicalis** due to recent specific studies regarding its unique **chromosomal plasticity**.
 
• **Aspergillus fumigatus:** This is a **mold**, not a yeast, and its resistance is typically linked to **environmental fungicide exposure** and specific **gene mutations** rather than broad chromosome alterations.
 
• **Cryptococcus neoformans:** An encapsulated yeast that causes **meningitis**; while it exhibits **aneuploidy**, its primary resistance mechanisms involve **capsule thickness** and **melanin production**.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Impact:** The rise of **multi-drug resistant (MDR)** fungal strains poses a severe threat to **immunocompromised patients**, such as those with **HIV/AIDS**, **cancer**, or those in **intensive care units (ICUs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aneuploidy:** This refers to the condition of having an **abnormal number** of chromosomes (e.g., **trisomy**). In **fungal pathogens**, it serves as a "quick-fix" evolutionary strategy to survive **environmental stress**.
 
• **Fluconazole Resistance:** It is often mediated by the **overexpression** of **MDR1** (Multidrug Resistance 1) genes, which act as **pumps** to remove the drug from the fungal cell.
 
• **Diagnostic Tools:** Recent advancements in **Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS)** have allowed scientists to map these **chromosomal changes** in real-time during a patient's treatment course, identifying how **Candida tropicalis** evolves within the **human body**.
 
• **Date and Discovery:** Research into the **genomic plasticity** of **Candida tropicalis** has gained significant momentum between **2020** and **2024**, revealing that **chromosomal instability** is a hallmark of its survival strategy.
</ul

• **Ronaldo** has been a mainstay for **Portugal** since his debut in **2003**, and this record adds to his extensive list of international accolades, including being the all-time leading goalscorer in international football.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In India, which High Court launched a dedicated portal for workplace sexual harassment complaints in July 2025 to empower women at work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Delhi High Court** achieved a significant milestone in judicial administration by launching a dedicated portal specifically designed for **workplace sexual harassment complaints**.
 
• The primary objective of this digital initiative is to empower **women at work**, including legal professionals, court staff, and litigants, by providing a secure and accessible platform to report grievances.
 
• This portal is integrated with the **Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)** of the High Court, ensuring that the process of filing and tracking complaints is handled with **confidentiality** and **speed**.
 
• By digitizing the complaint mechanism, the **Delhi High Court** aims to remove the barriers of physical presence and manual paperwork, fostering a **zero-tolerance policy** against harassment within the **judiciary's premises**.
 
• The launch of this portal aligns with the broader goals of the **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013**, reinforcing the legal framework for **gender safety** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The POSH Act, 2013**:
 
 
• The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act** was enacted in **2013** to provide protection against sexual harassment at workplaces and for the prevention and redressal of complaints.
 
• It mandates that any organization with **10 or more employees** must constitute an **Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)** to handle such matters.
 
 
 
• **Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)**:
 
 
• The **ICC** must be headed by a **Presiding Officer** who is a woman employed at a senior level in the workplace.
 
• It must also include an **external member** from an **NGO** or an association committed to the cause of women or a person familiar with issues relating to sexual harassment.
 
 
 
• **The Vishaka Guidelines**:
 
 
• Before the **2013 Act**, the **Supreme Court of India** laid down the **Vishaka Guidelines** in **1997** in the landmark case of **Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan**.
 
• These guidelines served as the legal framework for addressing sexual harassment until the formal **POSH Act** was legislated by **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **SHe-Box Portal**:
 
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development** launched the **Sexual Harassment electronic Box (SHe-Box)** as a single-window access to every woman, irrespective of her work status, to register complaints related to sexual harassment.
 
• This national-level portal ensures that complaints are directly reached to the concerned **authority** for timely action.
 
 
 
• **Digital Initiatives in Judiciary**:
 
 
• The **e-Courts Project**, conceptualized under the **National Policy and Action Plan for Implementation of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the Indian Judiciary**, has been pivotal in modernizing court functions.
 
• Portals like the one launched by the **Delhi High Court** are part of this **technological evolution** to make **justice delivery** more inclusive and transparent.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which state decided to review the Shakti Bill, which was to protect children and women from crime?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Maharashtra** government decided to review and update the **Shakti Criminal Laws (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill**.
 
• The **Shakti Bill** was originally passed by the **Maharashtra State Legislature** in **December 2021**, following the outrage over several heinous crimes against **women and children**.
 
• The decision to review the bill in **2025** stems from the need to align its provisions with the new central criminal laws—the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**—which replaced the **IPC** and **CrPC** in **July 2024**.
 
• The bill was modeled on the **Andhra Pradesh Disha Act** and aims to provide for the **death penalty** in cases of rape and gang rape, especially against children, and to speed up the judicial process.
 
• Because the bill seeks to amend criminal law (a **Concurrent List** subject), it requires **Presidential assent**; the **2025** review ensures that the amendments remain legally viable under the new **National Criminal Code** framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scope of Punishment**:
 
 
• The **Shakti Bill** proposes the **death penalty** or **life imprisonment** for the remainder of the natural life of the convict in cases of **rape, gang rape, and sexual assault** against minors.
 
• It also introduces a provision for a fine of up to **Rs. 10 lakh** for the perpetrator, which would be utilized for the victim's **medical expenses** and **rehabilitation**.
 
 
 
• **Expedited Investigation and Trial**:
 
 
• The bill mandates that the **investigation** of such crimes be completed within **15 working days** (extendable to 30 days under specific circumstances).
 
• The **trial** is expected to be concluded within **30 working days** from the date of filing the charge sheet, ensuring **swift justice** for the victims.
 
 
 
• **Special Units and Courts**:
 
 
• It proposes the establishment of **Special Police Teams** and **Special Courts** in each district of **Maharashtra** to handle cases related to the safety of **women and children**.
 
• The bill also addresses **cybercrimes**, proposing strict action against those who harass women via **social media** or digital platforms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Necessity**: The **2025** review is critical because many sections of the **IPC** and **CrPC** cited in the original **2021** draft no longer exist. Ensuring "concordance" with the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** is necessary for the bill to be enforceable once it receives the **President's signature**.
 
• **Joint Select Committee**: The draft of the bill had previously undergone rigorous scrutiny by a **Joint Select Committee** of the **Maharashtra State Legislature** before its initial passage to balance the rights of the accused with the safety of women.
 
• **Constitutional Framework**: Under **Article 254(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, a state law on a **Concurrent List** subject can override a central law only if it receives **Presidential assent**, making the current alignment process vital for **Maharashtra**.

questions.question: Which state/Union Territory observed its 25th Foundation Day on 9 November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Uttarakhand** celebrated its **25th Foundation Day** (Silver Jubilee) on **9 November 2025**. The state was officially carved out of **Uttar Pradesh** on **9 November 2000**, becoming the **27th state** of the Republic of India. 
 
• The formation of the state was the result of a long-standing **Uttarakhand statehood movement** that intensified in the **1990s**, demanding a separate administrative unit for the hilly regions to ensure better development and resource management. 
 
• Upon its creation, the state was named **Uttaranchal**. However, responding to the sentiments of the local population, the **Government of India** officially renamed it **Uttarakhand** in **January 2007**. 
 
• The state is divided into two main divisions, namely **Garhwal** and **Kumaon**, and it shares international boundaries with **China (Tibet)** to the north and **Nepal** to the east. 
 
• The legislative assembly of the state is located in **Dehradun** (winter capital), while **Gairsain** was officially declared the summer capital in **June 2020** to honor the aspirations of the hill people. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Chhattisgarh:** 
 
 
• It was formed on **1 November 2000**. It was carved out of the state of **Madhya Pradesh** to become the **26th state** of India. 
 
• The state was created primarily due to the distinct **cultural identity** and **socio-economic** needs of the tribal-dominated southeastern region of **Madhya Pradesh**. 
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand:** 
 
 
• It was established on **15 November 2000**, coinciding with the birth anniversary of the tribal leader **Birsa Munda**. It was separated from **Bihar** as the **28th state**. 
 
• The region is known as **'The Land of Forests'** and accounts for a significant portion of India’s **mineral wealth**, including coal and iron ore. 
 
 
 
• **Ladakh:** 
 
 
• It became a **Union Territory** on **31 October 2019**, following the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**, which bifurcated the erstwhile state of **Jammu and Kashmir**. 
 
• It is a **Union Territory without a legislature** and is known for its high-altitude cold desert landscape and strategic importance. 
 
 
 
• **State Reorganization Acts of 2000:** 
 
 
• The three new states (**Chhattisgarh**, **Uttarakhand**, and **Jharkhand**) were created under the **Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act**, **Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act**, and **Bihar Reorganisation Act** respectively, passed by the **Parliament** in the year **2000**. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Constitutional Provision:** The power to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing states is vested in the **Parliament of India** under **Article 3** of the **Constitution of India**. 
 
• **The Year 2000 Significance:** This **year** marked a major shift in India’s internal geography with the creation of three states in a single **month** (November). These formations were aimed at improving **administrative efficiency** and addressing **regional imbalances**. 
 
• **Geographical Identity:** **Uttarakhand** is often referred to as **Devbhumi** (Land of the Gods) due to the presence of numerous Hindu pilgrimage sites like **Badrinath**, **Kedarnath**, **Gangotri**, and **Yamunotri**. 

6f

questions.question: Which of the following organisations or ministries released the report titled ‘India’s Services Sector: Insights from GVA Trends and State-Level Dynamics’ in October 2025?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled **‘India’s Services Sector: Insights from GVA Trends and State-Level Dynamics’** was released by **NITI Aayog** in **October 2025** to provide a strategic roadmap for the tertiary sector.
 
• It focuses on the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** trends, highlighting how the services sector has become the primary engine of economic growth in India, contributing significantly to the national **GDP**.
 
• The report provides a detailed analysis of **state-level performance**, identifying top-performing states such as **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, and **Tamil Nadu** in terms of service output and innovation.
 
• One of the primary objectives of this publication is to address the **inter-state disparities** in service sector development and recommend policy measures to enhance **employment opportunities** and **export potential**.
 
• The document emphasizes the transition towards **knowledge-intensive services**, including **IT-BPM**, **Professional Services**, and **Financial Services**, which are pivotal for India's goal of becoming a **USD 5 trillion economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**
 
 
• Established on **1st January 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission** to foster **cooperative federalism**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** of India serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**, and it acts as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It focuses on long-term policy frameworks, monitoring and evaluation of government schemes, and promoting **innovation** through initiatives like the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**.
 
 
 
• **Services Sector in India:**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Tertiary Sector**, it encompasses a wide range of activities including **Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication, and Financial services**.
 
• In the **Indian economy**, the services sector typically contributes over **50%** of the total **Gross Value Added (GVA)**, making it the largest contributor among the three sectors.
 
• India is a global leader in **software exports** and **Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)**, significantly boosting the country's **Foreign Exchange Reserves**.
 
 
 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA):**
 
 
• **GVA** is defined as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption. It provides a measure of the contribution to **GDP** made by an individual producer, industry, or sector.
 
• It is a crucial metric used by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** to track economic activity from the supply side.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Digital Transformation:** The report highlights that the **Digital India** mission has played a transformative role in enabling **contactless services** and expanding the reach of **e-commerce** and **fintech** across rural and urban landscapes.
 
• **Employment Generation:** While the sector contributes high GVA, the report points out the need for **skill development** to ensure that the workforce can meet the demands of emerging technologies like **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Cloud Computing**.
 
• **FDI Inflows:** The **Computer Software and Hardware** and **Services** sectors consistently rank as the top recipients of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in India, showcasing global investor confidence.
 
• **Global Value Chains (GVCs):** **NITI Aayog** suggests that for India to improve its global standing, it must integrate more deeply into **Global Value Chains** by diversifying its service export basket beyond traditional IT services.

8f:T

questions.question: In February 2025, which athlete broke her own women’s 400 m National Games record, clocking 51.12 seconds to win gold?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

questions.question: Who among the following was leading the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) until March 2025, after which key reforms stalled?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Debasish Panda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Debasish Panda**, a **1987-batch** **IAS officer** of the **Uttar Pradesh** cadre, was appointed as the **Chairperson** of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in **March 2022**.
 
• His appointment was approved by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** for a tenure of **three years**, which concludes in **March 2025**.
 
• Before joining IRDAI, **Debasish Panda** served as the **Secretary** in the **Department of Financial Services (DFS)** under the **Ministry of Finance**, **Government of India**, where he retired in **January 2022**.
 
• Under his leadership, the regulatory body shifted its focus toward a **principle-based regime** rather than a rule-based one, aiming to enhance the **ease of doing business** in the insurance sector.
 
• He has been a key proponent of the vision **"Insurance for All by 2047"**, a mission intended to ensure that every citizen and enterprise in **India** has appropriate insurance coverage by the centenary of **Independence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About IRDAI:**
 
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** is a **statutory body** formed under the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999**.
 
• It functions as the apex body to regulate and develop the **insurance** and **re-insurance** industries in **India**.
 
• The body consists of a **10-member** team, including a **Chairman**, **five whole-time members**, and **four part-time members**, all appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• While it was initially headquartered in **New Delhi**, the head office was shifted to **Hyderabad**, **Telangana**, in **2001** to facilitate better regional administration.
 
 
 
• **Major Initiatives under current leadership:**
 
 
• **Bima Sugam:** This is a conceptualized **one-stop digital platform** designed to integrate all insurance stakeholders, including companies, agents, and consumers, to simplify the purchase and claim process.
 
• **Bima Vahak and Bima Vistaar:** These initiatives aim to reach the **rural** and **gram panchayat** levels to improve insurance **penetration** in under-served areas.
 
• **Risk-Based Capital (RBC):** IRDAI is working on transitioning from a factor-based solvency model to a **risk-based capital framework** to align Indian standards with **global** best practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Malhotra Committee:** The **IRDAI** was established following the recommendations of the **Malhotra Committee** report of **1994**, which suggested reforms to open up the insurance sector to private players.
 
• **Regulatory Duties:** As per **Section 14** of the **IRDA Act, 1999**, the authority is tasked with protecting the interests of **policyholders** and ensuring the orderly growth of the insurance market.
 
• **Other Options:** 
 
 
• **Sunil Mehta** is a prominent banker who served as the **Chief Executive** of the **Indian Banks' Association (IBA)**.
 
• **Subhash Chandra Khuntia** was the immediate **predecessor** of **Debasish Panda**, serving as **IRDAI Chairman** from **2018** to **2021**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, the seventh edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) took place. Which Indian state served as the host for these games?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **seventh edition** of the **Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG)** is scheduled to be hosted by the state of **Bihar** in **2025**. This marks the first time that Bihar has been selected to host this prestigious national-level multi-sport event.
 
• The announcement was made following the successful conclusion of previous editions, signaling the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports'** commitment to expanding sports infrastructure in the **eastern region** of India.
 
• The games are expected to feature over **30 sports disciplines**, with thousands of athletes in the **under-17** and **under-21** age categories participating from all **States** and **Union Territories** of India.
 
• Major venues for the **2025** games include the newly developed **State Sports Academy and Bihar Sports University** in **Rajgir**, as well as facilities in **Patna**. The **Rajgir Sports Complex** is designed to meet international standards to host diverse athletic events.
 
• Hosting **KIYG 2025** is a significant milestone for **Bihar**, aimed at promoting a sporting culture among the youth and identifying talent for future international competitions like the **Asian Games** and **Olympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of KIYG:**
 
 
• The **Khelo India Youth Games** (formerly Khelo India School Games) was launched in **2018** by the **Government of India**.
 
• The **first edition** was held in **New Delhi**, where **Haryana** emerged as the overall champion.
 
• Subsequent editions have been held in **Pune (2019)**, **Guwahati (2020)**, **Panchkula (2021/2022)**, **Madhya Pradesh (2023)**, and **Tamil Nadu (2024)**.

• **Other Khelo India Initiatives:**
 
 
• Apart from the Youth Games, the government conducts the **Khelo India University Games (KIUG)** to bridge the gap between school and professional sports.
 
• The **Khelo India Winter Games** are held in regions like **Gulmarg** and **Leh** to promote winter sports like skiing and ice hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Objective:** The primary goal of the **Khelo India** programme is to mass-participate and promote **excellence in sports**. It is a central sector scheme fully funded by the **Central Government**.
 
• **Governance:** The initiative is overseen by the **Department of Sports** under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, currently headed by the Union Sports Minister.
 
• **Bihar's Preparation:** To prepare for the **2025 games**, the **Bihar** government has emphasized the "**Medal Lao, Naukri Pao**" (Bring Medal, Get Job) policy to incentivize local athletes and has increased the **sports budget** significantly for infrastructure development.

questions.question: India launched its National Red List Roadmap at which of the following international events in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IUCN World Conservation Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India officially launched its **National Red List Roadmap** during the **IUCN World Conservation Congress (WCC)** held in **2025**. This roadmap serves as a strategic document to guide the assessment of the conservation status of species found within **India**.
 
• The initiative is a collaborative effort led by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, in partnership with global conservation bodies. It aims to apply the **IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria** at the national level to identify species at the highest risk of **extinction**.
 
• The primary objective of the **National Red List Roadmap** is to ensure that conservation efforts are data-driven. By creating a national database, India can prioritize funding and protection for species classified as **Critically Endangered** or **Endangered** under national standards.
 
• This roadmap is crucial for fulfilling India’s obligations under the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**, specifically **Target 4**, which focuses on halting species extinction and managing human-wildlife conflict.
 
• The **2025 Congress** in **Abu Dhabi, UAE**, provided the international platform for India to showcase its scientific rigor in biodiversity monitoring, involving organizations like the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)** and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is IUCN World Conservation Congress.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature):** 
 
 
• Established in **1948**, it is the world’s largest environmental network, composed of both **government** and **civil society** organizations.
 
• Its headquarters is located in **Gland, Switzerland**. The organization acts as an advisor to the **United Nations** and helps implement international conventions.
 
 
 
• **IUCN Red List of Threatened Species:** 
 
 
• First established in **1964**, it is the global standard for evaluating the extinction risk of species. It classifies species into categories such as **Vulnerable**, **Endangered**, and **Critically Endangered**.
 
• The **Red List** is updated periodically and serves as a "health check" for the planet's **biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **IUCN World Conservation Congress (WCC):** 
 
 
• This event is held every **four years** and is often referred to as the "Olympics of Conservation." The **2025** session in **Abu Dhabi** focused heavily on **nature-based solutions** and **climate resilience**.
 
• It brings together thousands of delegates to vote on **motions** that set the global agenda for conservation policy.
 
 
 
• **National Red List vs. Global Red List:** 
 
 
• While the global list assesses species across their entire range, a **National Red List** focuses on the status of a species within a specific country's **borders**.
 
• A species might be **Least Concern** globally but **Critically Endangered** within India due to localized threats like **habitat loss** or **poaching**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biodiversity in India:** India is recognized as one of the **17 mega-diverse** countries in the world, harboring approximately **7-8%** of all recorded species. Notable endemics include the **Asiatic Lion** and the **Sangai Deer**.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The data generated through the **National Red List Roadmap** will inform the schedules of the **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972**, ensuring legal protection matches the biological threat level.
 
• **Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF):** Adopted in **2022**, the framework sets **23 targets** for **2030**, including the protection of **30%** of the world’s land and oceans (the **30x30 target**).
 
• **Other Options Context:** The **UN Climate Change Conference (COP30)** in **Brazil** primarily focuses on **carbon emissions** and the **Paris Agreement**, whereas the **IUCN WCC** is specifically dedicated to **species conservation**.

questions.question: The Eravikulam National Park, which emerged as one of the two top-performing protected areas in India in the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) conducted by the Wildlife Institute of India in June 2025, is home to which of the following species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nilgiri Tahr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eravikulam National Park (ENP)** is situated in the **Devikulam Taluk** of **Idukki district** in **Kerala**, along the high ranges of the **Southern Western Ghats**.
 
• It is famously known as the natural habitat of the **Nilgiri Tahr** (***Nilgiritragus hylocrius***), an endangered mountain goat that is endemic to the **Western Ghats**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nilgiri Tahr.***
 
• In **June 2025**, the park was recognized by the **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** in its **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** report as one of the top-performing protected areas in the country due to its excellence in biodiversity conservation and administrative efficiency.
 
• The park houses **Anamudi**, which is the **highest peak** in **South India**, standing at an elevation of **2,695 metres**.
 
• Originally established as a **wildlife sanctuary** in **1975** primarily to protect the declining population of the **Nilgiri Tahr**, it was elevated to the status of a **National Park** in **1978**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vegetation and Flora:**
 
 
• The park's ecosystem is characterized by **high-altitude grasslands** interspersed with **Shola forests** (stunted tropical montane forests).
 
• It is one of the primary sites for the blooming of the **Neelakurinji** (***Strobilanthes kunthiana***), a flower that carpets the hills in blue once every **12 years**.
 
 
 
• **Faunal Diversity:**
 
 
• Apart from the flagship **Nilgiri Tahr**, the park is home to other species like the **Gaur**, **Indian Muntjac**, **Sambar Deer**, **Golden Jackal**, and **Leopard**.
 
• The **Lion-tailed Macaque** is another endemic species of the **Western Ghats**, but it is more commonly associated with the **Silent Valley National Park** rather than the grassland-dominant terrain of **Eravikulam**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrography:**
 
 
• The park serves as a major catchment area for several perennial streams that feed into the **Periyar River** and the **Chalakuddy River**.
 
 
 
• **Tourism:**
 
 
• The **Rajamala** region is the designated tourism zone within the park where visitors are allowed to witness the **Nilgiri Tahr** at close quarters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Status of Nilgiri Tahr:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is listed as **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List**.
 
• It is protected under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, providing it the highest level of legal protection in **India**.
 
• The **Government of Tamil Nadu** has also launched **Project Nilgiri Tahr** (the first of its kind) to protect its state animal, which shares its habitat with **Kerala's** high-altitude zones.
 
 
 
• **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE):**
 
 
• **MEE** is a global framework used by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** and **WII** to assess how well protected areas are being managed.
 
• The **2025** evaluation highlights **Eravikulam's** success in maintaining a healthy "population-to-habitat" ratio and mitigating human-wildlife conflict.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), which of the following city-states signed a “Comprehensive Strategic Partnership” with India, including MoUs in semiconductors, digital technology and skills development in September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Singapore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the official visit of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** to **Singapore** in **September 2024**, India and **Singapore** elevated their bilateral relationship to a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**.
 
• This elevation marks a significant milestone in the **India-Singapore** relationship, aimed at deepening cooperation across various high-tech and emerging sectors to meet the needs of the **21st century**.
 
• A total of **four Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** were signed, covering **Semiconductors**, **Digital Technologies**, **Health and Medicine**, and **Skill Development and Education**.
 
• The **MoU** on **Semiconductors**, signed by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** of India and **Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry**, focuses on establishing a robust semiconductor ecosystem and supply chain resilience.
 
• The **Digital Technology** agreement aims to enhance cooperation in **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**, **Cyber Security**, and **5G/6G** technologies, while the **Skill Development** MoU focuses on **Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Ties:** **Singapore** is one of India's largest sources of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**. In the financial year **2023-24**, it was the leading source of **FDI** equity inflows into India, contributing approximately **$11.77 billion**.
 
• **Digital Connectivity:** India and **Singapore** successfully linked their fast payment systems, **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** and **PayNow**, in **February 2023**, enabling instant and low-cost cross-border fund transfers.
 
• **Defense Cooperation:** The two nations share strong defense ties, including the **SIMBEX** (Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise), which is the longest uninterrupted naval exercise India has with any other country, beginning in **1994**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** **Singapore** serves as a vital pillar of India's **"Act East" Policy** and plays a crucial role in India's engagement with the **ASEAN** (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR):** The **ISMR** is a unique mechanism designed to set a new agenda for bilateral relations. The **second edition** of the **ISMR** held in **August 2024** paved the way for the **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**.
 
• **Semiconductor Hub:** **Singapore** accounts for roughly **10%** of the global semiconductor output and **20%** of semiconductor equipment production, making it a critical partner for India's **India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)**.
 
• **Leadership:** The agreements were finalized during discussions between Indian PM **Narendra Modi** and Singapore PM **Lawrence Wong** at the **Parliament House** in **Singapore**.
 
• **Ministry Involvement:** The **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** coordinated the diplomatic elevation, while **MeitY** specifically led the technological partnerships in the **digital** and **semiconductor** domains.

questions.question: Which Glaswegian author released Hermit in 2025, dealing with themes of toxic masculinity and online misogyny?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chris McQueer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chris McQueer** is a prominent **Glaswegian** author and screenwriter known for his unique voice in contemporary **Scottish literature**.
 
• In **January 2025**, he released his debut full-length novel titled **Hermit**, which explores the dark and claustrophobic world of **online radicalization**.
 
• The novel focuses on the themes of **toxic masculinity** and the rise of **online misogyny**, specifically looking at the "manosphere" and incel culture through the eyes of the protagonist, **Cillian**.
 
• The story is set in **Glasgow**, providing a gritty, realistic backdrop to the character's descent into digital isolation and harmful ideologies.
 
• McQueer uses the narrative to dissect how **social media algorithms** and **internet subcultures** can distort a young man's perception of reality and relationships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chris McQueer** first gained critical acclaim with his short story collections, **Hings** (**2017**) and **HWFG** (**2018**), which were celebrated for their use of the **Scots language** and surrealist humor.
 
• His work often highlights the **working-class experience** in **Scotland**, blending everyday situations with bizarre, often dark, twists.
 
• The novel **Hermit** was published by **4th Estate**, an imprint of **HarperCollins**, marking a significant milestone in McQueer's transition from short fiction to long-form novels.
 
• Other authors mentioned, such as **Ocean Vuong**, are known for different literary traditions; Vuong is a **Vietnamese-American** poet and novelist famous for **On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous**.
 
• **Margaret McDonald** is a fellow **Scottish** author whose debut novel, **Glasgow Boys**, was released in **2024** and also deals with **masculinity** and male friendship in **Glasgow**, though it focuses on different thematic elements than **Hermit**.
 
• **Nell Stevens** is a **British** author known for **Briefly, A Delicious Life** and **Mrs. Gaskell and Me**, whose work typically focuses on historical and biographical fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The release of **Hermit** in **2025** is considered a timely intervention in literature, addressing the real-world consequences of **loneliness** and the **internet**.
 
• **Chris McQueer** has also worked in **television**, adapting his short stories for **BBC Scotland**, which has helped bring his **Glaswegian** narratives to a wider audience.
 
• The term **incel** (involuntary celibate) and the concept of the **manosphere** are central to the book's investigation into modern **social isolation**.
 
• The author’s move away from purely comedic short stories toward a more serious exploration of **misogyny** and **masculinity** shows the evolution of his writing style.
